column3: Current clock event (throttle) reasons; bitmask (nvmlClocksEventReasons_t). 11 bits: 0x001 GPU_IDLE; 0x002 APP_CLOCKS; 0x004 SW_POWER_CAP; 0x008 HW_SLOWDOWN; 0x010 SYNC_BOOST; 0x020 SW_THERMAL; 0x040 HW_THERMAL; 0x080 HW_POWER_BRAKE; 0x100 DISPLAY_CLOCKS; 0x200 BOARD_LIMIT; 0x400 RELIABILITY (undocumented in dcgm_fields.h but real -- confirmed via nvidia-smi -q -d PERFORMANCE). column3: Per-subsystem GPU health check result (0 = pass; 10 = warn; 20 = fail -- dcgmHealthWatchResults_t). One series per 'health_watch' label (PCIE/NVLINK/PMU/MCU/MEM/SM/INFOROM/THERMAL/POWER/DRIVER/ALL). Dense: always emits; including a 0/pass value; for every watch on every GPU -- confirmed via exporter source (initGPUHealthEntityIncidentDefaults). The 'ALL' label is DCGM's own separate GPU-wide watch; NOT a rollup/derived value of the other 10 -- it independently reports devastating faults with no single named subsystem (e.g. Xid 79 fallen off bus; Xid 95 uncontained ECC; confirmed via exporter source: gpuHealthChecks lists DCGM_HEALTH_WATCH_ALL as its own entry). Include it in any 'is this GPU healthy' aggregation alongside the other 10 -- max()/max by(...) is idempotent under duplication; this can only surface a failure the other 10 would have missed; never a double-count.

Count of distinct XID events observed in a trailing window (default 5 min). Always emits; including a 0-valued series when healthy -- confirmed dense via exporter source; safe to alert/graph directly; unlike the sparse field below.

Running total of XID events per code since the exporter started. Sparse: no series exists at all for a given 'xid' label until that code has fired at least once -- treat 'no data' as 'never happened'; not as an error.
